subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: Your wardrobe faces the bed with a modest gap between them. Which doors would you live with?
ig:
Your wardrobe faces the bed with a modest gap between them. Which doors would you live with?

This is the most common layout we are asked about, and both choices have a cost.

A: Sliding doors
They never swing into the room, so the walkway stays clear even with the doors open. The cost: you only see part of the wardrobe at a time, and internal drawers have to be planned around the overlap.

B: Hinged doors
Open two doors and the whole wardrobe is in front of you, with drawers wherever you want them. The cost: each door needs clear floor to swing, so a tight gap means doors that knock the bed or a shuffle to get past.

There is no wrong answer, just the trade-off you would rather live with every morning.

A or B? Tell us the rough gap you have and what you mostly store, and we will tell you which we would lean towards.
fb:
Here is a bedroom puzzle a lot of people will recognise: the wardrobe is on the wall facing the bed, and the gap between them is not huge.

Sliding doors keep that walkway clear, but you only ever open half the wardrobe. Hinged doors open everything up, but need room to swing. Neither is wrong, it just depends on which compromise suits you.

Which would you choose, A or B? Pop your answer and the rough gap you have in the comments, and we will give you our honest take. See our fitted wardrobes here:
